title: Savanna Friends!
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Milo the bluebird, and welcome to The Animated Zoo!
Today we're visiting five amazing savanna animals. Every animal has a super surprise.
Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!

lines: Here's our first animal. Here's a clue: it has a very, very long neck! Can you guess?
Giraffes are the tallest animals in the whole world.
Their long necks help them reach leaves high up in the trees.
A baby giraffe is already about as tall as a grown-up when it's born!
Can you stretch up tall like a giraffe? Reach up high! Stretch, stretch!
Can you guess what color a giraffe's tongue is?
It's purple! And it can be up to twenty inches long.
Scientists think the dark color helps protect it from the hot sun.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it has big ears and a long trunk! Can you guess?
Next, let's stomp over to the elephants!
Elephants are the biggest animals on land.
An elephant's trunk is its nose and its top lip, all in one!
Elephants flap their big ears to help them cool down.
Can you swing your arm like an elephant trunk? Swing, swing!
Can you guess? Can elephants jump?
No! Their legs stand straight, like strong tree trunks, to hold up their heavy bodies.
But elephants love water, and they are good swimmers!
Who's next? Here's a clue: it has a big fluffy mane and a loud roar! Can you guess?
Now, let's tiptoe to the lions. Shh!
Lions live together in a family group called a pride.
Mommy lions work together to find food for the whole family.
Can you do a tiny lion roar? Ready? Roar!
Can you guess how far away you can hear a lion's roar?
Up to five miles away! That's really, really far.
Lions also love to nap. They can sleep up to twenty hours a day!
So at the zoo, we stay quiet and let the lions rest.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it has black and white stripes! Can you guess?
Zebras are part of the horse family.
Every zebra has its own special stripes. No two zebras are the same, just like your fingerprints!
Zebras can sleep standing up, while their friends keep watch.
Can you gallop like a zebra? Gallop, gallop, gallop!
Can you guess what color a zebra's skin is, under its fur?
It's dark! Zebras have dark skin under their black and white stripes.
A baby zebra learns its mom's stripes, so it can always find her.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it loves to splash in the water, and it has a giant mouth! Can you guess?
Splash! Now we're at the hippo pool.
Hippos spend most of the day in the water to stay cool.
Hippos can hold their breath under the water for a few minutes.
Can you open your mouth super wide like a hippo? Ahhh!
Can you guess? Can hippos swim?
Not really! Hippos walk and bounce along the bottom of the river.
Hippos even make their own sunscreen. Their skin makes a special red-orange goo.

recap: Wow, what an adventure! Let's remember.
Elephants can't jump, but they can swim.
You can hear a lion roar from five miles away.
Every zebra has its own stripes.
And hippos make their own sunscreen!
outro: Which animal was your favorite? Remember, be kind to every animal. Watch quietly and give them space.
Bye, friends! See you at the zoo!
